elements.element: Contractor's maximum liability amount is the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 7(a) applies that exact greater-of formula to Contractor's cap, although the existing cap remains limited to liability relating to performance of services under a Statement of Work.

elements.element: Company's maximum liability amount is the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Company's cap remains the amount of fees paid to Contractor, with no 12-month lookback, payable-fees component, or USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 7(b) provides that neither party is liable to the other for indirect or consequential damages, as well as specified additional damage categories.

elements.element: Liability for either party's breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breach of a party's confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim, and paragraph 7(a)'s caps do not apply to Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for either party's breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breach of a party's data protection obligations is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for either party's breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breach of a party's security obligations is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for either party's indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's indemnification obligations are expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability arising from either party's gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's gross negligence is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability arising from either party's wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's wilful misconduct is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability arising from either party's fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's fraud is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability arising from either party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not damages for cap purposes.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Customer's payment obligations, with Company identified as Customer, are not damages.

elements.element: Contractor's maximum liability amount is 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: Contractor's cap is the greater of 12 months' paid or payable fees and USD 1,000,000, so it may exceed 12 months' fees.

elements.element: Company's maximum liability amount is 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: Company's cap remains all fees paid to Contractor and contains no 12-month limitation.

elements.element: Liability for either party's indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims to which paragraph 7(a)'s caps do not apply.

elements.element: Liability for either party's breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality breaches are Excluded Claims to which paragraph 7(a)'s caps do not apply.

elements.element: Liability arising from either party's gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is an Excluded Claim to which paragraph 7(a)'s caps do not apply.

elements.element: Liability arising from either party's wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is an Excluded Claim to which paragraph 7(a)'s caps do not apply.

result.reason: The carve-outs, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and Customer-payment classification are operative, but the cap amount was changed only for Contractor. Company's cap therefore satisfies neither the preferred formula nor the fallback 12-month-fees formulation; Contractor's greater-of cap also does not equal the fallback cap. The drafting is not minimal because it fails to reach either complete position and unnecessarily states that all amounts due under the Agreement—not only Customer's payment obligations—are not damages. That overbreadth may affect amounts owed by Contractor and departs from the intended party direction.
